title: A Promise does not run later — it queues a microtask
thesis: then callbacks run after the current call stack, before the next macrotask — so they can starve timers if you keep chaining.
problem: Thinking Promise is 'async like setTimeout' puts then() after paint and timers. It is not.
whyNotBasic: A macrotask delay would let the browser paint between each then. The spec chose a microtask checkpoint instead.
cost: A tight then-chain can delay rendering. You pay with queueMicrotask discipline.

asides.title: When the checkpoint runs
asides.body: After the running script returns, the engine drains the microtask queue before the next task (timer, I/O, click). `queueMicrotask` and `Promise.then` share that queue. A then that enqueues another then keeps the checkpoint busy.

steps.title: Create while the stack runs
steps.narration: Promise.resolve during a script does not call then yet. It only records the reaction. [[checkpoint]]

steps.title: Enqueue a microtask
steps.narration: The then reaction is a microtask, not a timer. It sits on the same queue as queueMicrotask.

steps.title: Drain before the next task
steps.narration: When the stack is empty, the engine drains microtasks. Timers wait.

steps.title: A chain can starve paint
steps.narration: Each then that schedules another then extends the checkpoint. The timer still has not run.
